Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a complex problem by calling smaller, identical instances of itself. Think of it like opening a set of Russian nesting dolls, where each doll reveals a slightly smaller version inside until you reach the solid center. To prevent an endless loop, every recursive function requires a "base case," which serves as a strict stopping condition that provides an immediate answer. Once that base condition is reached, the function systematically resolves each previous layer in reverse order to assemble the final result.
